div.head: V Atr 7
div.ab: ⁊ canónicas, þær seo ár sy, þæt hy beoddern ⁊ slæpern habban magan, healdan heora mynster mid rihte ⁊ mid clænnesse, swa heora regol tæce; oððon riht is, þæt þolige þære are se ðe þæt nelle.
⁊ canonicas, þær seo ár sy, þæt hy beoddern ⁊ slæpern habban magon, healdan heora mynster mid rihte ⁊ mid clænnesse, swa heora regol tæce; oððon riht is, þæt þolige þæ þære are se þe þæt nelle.
And canonicas, þar seo ár sý, þæt hi beoddern ⁊ slæpern habban magan, healdan heora mynster mid rihte ⁊ mid clænnisse, swa heora regol tæce; oððe riht is, þæt he þolige þare are se ðe þæt nelle.
And canonicas þar seo ár sý þæt hi beoddern ⁊ slæpern habban magan, healdan heora mynster mid rihte ⁊ mid clænnisse, swa heora regol tæce; oððe riht is þæt he þolige þare are se ðe þæt nelle.
And canonicas, þær seo ar sy þæt hy beoddern and slæpern habban magan, healdan heora mynster mid rihte and mid clænnesse, swa heora regol tæce; oððon riht is, þæt þolige þære are se ðe þæt nelle.

Und Kanoniker, wo solcher Kirchenbesitz vorhanden ist, dass sie [gemeinsamen] Speisesaal und Schlafsaal haben können, sollen ihr Stift gesetzmässig und in Keuschheit halten, wie ihre Regel vorschreibt; oder richtig ist, dass, wer dies nicht will, die Pfründe verliere.

And canons, where there is such church property that they can have a [common] refectory and dormitory, are to keep their foundation lawfully and in chastity, as their rule prescribes; otherwise it is right that whoever will not do this lose the benefice.

And canons, wherever their property admits of their having a refectory and a dormitory, shall maintain regularity and celibacy in their foundation, as their rule prescribes; otherwise it is right that he who refuses to do so should forfeit his endowment.

And canons, where there is property such that they can have a refectory and dormitory, are to hold their minster with right observance and with chastity, as their rule directs; otherwise it is right that he who will not do that shall forfeit the property.

And canons, when their holding is such that they possess a refectory and a dormitory, shall hold their monastery with propriety and celibacy, just as their rule instructs; or else he who will not do that must forfeit his holding.
div.note: Liebermann prints G without ‘he’ (D has ‘he’); G2 has a dittography ‘þæ’. Liebermann compares I As 4.

Es gab auch ausser den Kathedralstiftern Konventualen mit Weltgeistlichen; Stubbs Foundation of Waltham p. VI
Besides the cathedral chapters there were also conventual communities of secular clergy; Stubbs Foundation of Waltham p. VI
‘Kloster’ Schmid, doch waren Kanoniker nicht Mönche
‘rein’ Schmid, aber in solchem Zusammenhange stets engeren Sinnes; durch clænness wird coelibatus glossiert; Toller Suppl.
‘pure’ (Schmid), but in such a context it always has the narrower sense; clænness is used to gloss coelibatus; Toller Suppl.
‘Grundbesitz’ Schmid, in eigenem Besitz, im Ggs. zum Mönch; vgl. Geistliche 12. 20
‘landed property’ (Schmid); i.e. in their own possession, in contrast to the monk; cf. Geistliche 12. 20

This is the first occurrence of the term ‘canon’ in the Laws and, apart from this context, it appears in only one other clause, viz. VI 2 (where V 4 reads preostas) repeated in I Cn. 6 a (see further J. Armitage Robinson, St Oswald and the Church of Worcester, Supplemental Papers of the British Academy, p. 13, and The Times of St Dunstan, pp. 170–1).
I understand that the question of the position of canons in the Early Church will be discussed by Miss M. Deanesly in an article on The Familia at Christchurch, Canterbury, 597–832, in the forthcoming presentation volume to Professor T. F. Tout.
Presumably the prebend which came to him in virtue of his position.
